_what: [CORPUS-BASELINE] Corpus checks that already fail, so scheduled CI can report them without blocking merges. This is a RATCHET, not an excuse list.
_rules: Every entry names a tracked issue. No entry without one.
Adding an entry is admitting a defect shipped. Fixing it and deleting the entry is the only correct exit.
Anything NOT listed here fails CI even in baseline mode — that is the regression gate.
`make test-corpus` locally ignores this file entirely and fails on everything. Local runs stay honest.
Check ids are rank-independent on purpose: #301 moves cluster ranks between runs, so a rank-bearing key would churn.

_checks.recall: A hand-verified duplicate was not reported (false negative).
_checks.boilerplate_rank: Framework-mandated scaffolding ranked in the top N.
_checks.data_table_rank: A numeric data table ranked in the top N categorised as `logic`.
_checks.memory: Peak RSS exceeded the runner budget.
_checks.fused_bounded_max: A rendered confidence exceeded the strongest single axis it was computed from, which [FUSION-STRATEGY-BOUNDED-MAX] forbids — the sum-then-clamp saturation gh #343 removed, pinned as an exact per-cluster formula rather than as a distribution.
_checks.type2_gate_liveness: A large same-shape population was demoted and not one visible cluster reached `nearly_identical` through the gate's own saturating-shape precondition ([FUSION-CONTENT-GATE]). A population-shape heuristic, not a recall assertion: it identifies no expected pair. `identical` does not count (decided by byte equivalence before the gate runs) and neither does a sub-floor token near-miss (classified by the ordinary Type-3 path without the gate judging it).
_checks.type2_recall: A hand-verified Type-2 rename curated in the manifest's `must_find_type2` was not reported as a shown, gate-vouched `nearly_identical` cluster spanning its files. A hidden occurrence on either curated side is a miss: recall is what the report shows, not what it contains — a false negative on known rename ground truth ([CORPUS-RECALL]).
